337	def _validate_link(identifier: str, field: str, type_name: str) -> None:
338	    if identifier_type(identifier) != type_name:
339	        raise ValidationError(
340	            f"{field} must reference a {type_name} object, got {identifier_type(identifier)}"
341	        )
342	
343	
344	# Relationship endpoints this release accepts: an indicator points at the identity
345	# that published the intelligence, which mirrors how `indicates` is used in the wild.
346	RELATIONSHIP_LINKS = (("source_ref", "indicator"), ("target_ref", "identity"))
347	
348	
349	@dataclass(frozen=True)
350	class StixObject:
351	    """One validated STIX 2.1 object ready to be stored in a collection."""
352	
353	    type: str
354	    id: str
355	    created: str
356	    modified: str
357	    properties: dict[str, Any]
358	
359	    @classmethod
360	    def parse(cls, raw: Any) -> "StixObject":
361	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
362	            raise ValidationError("STIX object body must be a JSON object")
363	        type_name = raw.get("type")
364	        if type_name not in OBJECT_TYPES:
365	            raise ValidationError(
366	                "type must be one of " + ", ".join(OBJECT_TYPES)
367	            )
368	        allowed = set(COMMON_PROPERTIES) | set(TYPE_PROPERTIES[type_name])
369	        unknown = sorted(set(raw) - allowed)
370	        if unknown:
371	            raise ValidationError(
372	                f"{type_name} has unsupported properties: {', '.join(unknown)}"
373	            )
374	        if raw.get("spec_version", SPEC_VERSION) != SPEC_VERSION:
375	            raise ValidationError("spec_version must be 2.1")
376	
377	        if not isinstance(raw.get("id"), str):
378	            raise ValidationError("id is required")
379	        identifier = validate_identifier(raw["id"], "id")
380	        if identifier_type(identifier) != ID_PREFIX[type_name]:
381	            raise ValidationError(
382	                f"id {identifier} does not match type {type_name}; "
383	                f"expected the {ID_PREFIX[type_name]}--<uuid> form"
384	            )
385	
386	        for name in ("created", "modified"):
387	            if name not in raw:
388	                raise ValidationError(f"{name} is required")
389	        created = canonical_timestamp(raw["created"], "created")
390	        modified = canonical_timestamp(raw["modified"], "modified")
391	        if timestamp_value(modified) < timestamp_value(created):
392	            raise ValidationError("modified must not be earlier than created")
393	
394	        properties: dict[str, Any] = {"type": type_name, "id": identifier, "spec_version": SPEC_VERSION}
395	        for name, kind in COMMON_PROPERTIES.items():
396	            if name in ("type", "id", "created", "modified"):
397	                continue
398	            if name in raw:
399	                properties[name] = _validate_property(raw[name], kind, name)
400	        for name, kind in TYPE_PROPERTIES[type_name].items():
401	            if name in raw:
402	                properties[name] = _validate_property(raw[name], kind, name)
403	
404	        for name in REQUIRED_PROPERTIES[type_name]:
405	            if name not in raw:
406	                raise ValidationError(f"{type_name} requires the {name} property")
407	
408	        if type_name == "indicator":
409	            if properties.get("pattern_type", "stix") != "stix":
410	                raise ValidationError("only pattern_type stix is supported")
411	            properties["pattern_type"] = "stix"
412	        if type_name == "relationship":
413	            cls._validate_relationship(properties)
414	        if type_name == "note":
415	            cls._validate_note(identifier, properties)
416	        return cls(type_name, identifier, created, modified, properties)
417	
418	    @staticmethod
419	    def _validate_note(identifier: str, properties: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
420	        # object_refs is structurally validated above; the one rule that needs the
421	        # note's own id is that a note may not annotate itself.
422	        if identifier in properties["object_refs"]:
423	            raise ValidationError("note object_refs must not reference the note itself")
424	
425	    @staticmethod
426	    def _validate_relationship(properties: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
427	        source = properties["source_ref"]
428	        target = properties["target_ref"]
429	        if source == target:
430	            raise ValidationError("source_ref and target_ref must differ")
431	        _validate_link(source, *RELATIONSHIP_LINKS[0])
432	        _validate_link(target, *RELATIONSHIP_LINKS[1])
433	        if "start_time" in properties and "stop_time" in properties:
434	            if timestamp_value(properties["stop_time"]) < timestamp_value(properties["start_time"]):
435	                raise ValidationError("stop_time must not be earlier than start_time")
436	
437	    def document(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
438	        document = dict(self.properties)
439	        document["created"] = self.created
440	        document["modified"] = self.modified
441	        return document
442	
443	    def references(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
444	        if self.type == "relationship":
445	            return (self.properties["source_ref"], self.properties["target_ref"])
446	        if self.type in ("report", "note"):
447	            return tuple(self.properties["object_refs"])
448	        return ()
449	
450	    @property
451	    def revoked(self) -> bool:
452	        """Whether this version revokes the object; an omitted flag means false."""
453	        return bool(self.properties.get("revoked", False))
454	
455	    def version_key(self) -> str:
456	        """The TAXII version identifier of this revision."""
457	        return self.modified

13	    def __init__(self, path: str):
14	        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
15	        self.connection = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
16	        self.connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
17	        self.connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
18	        self.connection.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
19	        self.connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
20	        self.connection.executescript(
21	            """
22	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collections (
23	              id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
24	              document TEXT NOT NULL
25	            );
26	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS objects (
27	              collection_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES collections(id),
28	              object_id TEXT NOT NULL,
29	              version TEXT NOT NULL,
30	              type TEXT NOT NULL,
31	              added_at TEXT NOT NULL,
32	              document TEXT NOT NULL,
33	              PRIMARY KEY (collection_id, object_id, version)
34	            );
35	            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS objects_delta
36	              ON objects(collection_id, added_at, object_id);
37	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS idempotency (
38	              key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
39	              operation TEXT NOT NULL,
40	              response TEXT NOT NULL,
41	              status INTEGER NOT NULL
42	            );
43	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
44	              id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
45	              collection_id TEXT NOT NULL,
46	              created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
47	              limit_value INTEGER NOT NULL,
48	              type_filter TEXT
49	            );
50	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshot_entries (
51	              snapshot_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
52	              position INTEGER NOT NULL,
53	              document TEXT NOT NULL,
54	              PRIMARY KEY (snapshot_id, position)
55	            );
56	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (
57	              key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
58	              value TEXT NOT NULL
59	            );
60	            """
61	        )
62	        self.cursor_secret = self._load_secret()
63	
64	    def _load_secret(self) -> bytes:
65	        """Return the persistent secret used to sign page cursors."""
66	        row = self.connection.execute(
67	            "SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key = 'cursor_secret'"
68	        ).fetchone()
69	        if row is not None:
70	            return bytes.fromhex(row["value"])
71	        secret = os.urandom(32)
72	        self.connection.execute(
73	            "INSERT INTO meta(key, value) VALUES ('cursor_secret', ?)",
74	            (secret.hex(),),
75	        )
76	        return secret

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from stixrelay.errors import ConflictError, ForbiddenError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
from stixrelay.model import MEDIA_TYPE
from stixrelay.service import NDJSON_MEDIA_TYPE, StixRelay

IDENTITY_ID = "identity--f431f809-377b-45e0-aa1c-6a4751cae5ff"
INDICATOR_ID = "indicator--a2f4b7d8-2c7e-4a4b-9d0e-6f6a1c9d3f21"
MALWARE_ID = "malware--3c9d1e4f-5a6b-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f"
RELATIONSHIP_ID = "relationship--b6a1e2c3-1f2a-4b3c-8d4e-5f6a7b8c9d0e"
REPORT_ID = "report--c7d8e9f0-1a2b-4c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f"
REPORT2_ID = "report--d8e9f012-3b4c-4d5e-9f50-6a7b8c9d0e1f"
NOTE_ID = "note--9fb2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"
NOTE2_ID = "note--a0c3d4e5-f6a7-4b8c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e"

CREATED = "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
REPORT_PUBLISHED = "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"


def identity(*, modified: str = CREATED, name: str = "Example Org") -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "identity",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": IDENTITY_ID,
        "created": CREATED,
        "modified": modified,
        "name": name,
        "identity_class": "organization",
    }


def indicator(*, modified: str = CREATED, pattern: str = "[file:hashes.'SHA-256' = 'aa']") -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "indicator",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": INDICATOR_ID,
        "created": CREATED,
        "modified": modified,
        "name": "Bad hash",
        "pattern": pattern,
        "pattern_type": "stix",
        "valid_from": CREATED,
    }


def malware(*, modified: str = CREATED) -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "malware",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": MALWARE_ID,
        "created": CREATED,
        "modified": modified,
        "name": "Loader",
        "is_family": True,
        "malware_types": ["trojan"],
    }


def relationship(*, modified: str = CREATED) -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "relationship",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": RELATIONSHIP_ID,
        "created": CREATED,
        "modified": modified,
        "relationship_type": "indicates",
        "source_ref": INDICATOR_ID,
        "target_ref": IDENTITY_ID,
    }


def report(
    *,
    modified: str = CREATED,
    object_refs: list[str] | None = None,
    published: str = REPORT_PUBLISHED,
    report_id: str = REPORT_ID,
) -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "report",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": report_id,
        "created": CREATED,
        "modified": modified,
        "name": "Monthly report",
        "description": "What happened this month",
        "published": published,
        "report_types": ["threat-report"],
        "object_refs": [INDICATOR_ID, IDENTITY_ID] if object_refs is None else object_refs,
    }


def revoked(payload: dict) -> dict:
    body = dict(payload)
    body["revoked"] = True
    return body


def note(
    *,
    modified: str = CREATED,
    content: str = "Analyst comment",
    object_refs: list[str] | None = None,
    note_id: str = NOTE_ID,
    abstract: str | object = None,
    authors: list[str] | object = None,
) -> dict:
    payload = {
        "type": "note",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": note_id,
        "created": CREATED,
        "modified": modified,
        "content": content,
        "object_refs": [INDICATOR_ID] if object_refs is None else object_refs,
    }
    if abstract is not None:
        payload["abstract"] = abstract
    if authors is not None:
        payload["authors"] = authors
    return payload


class StixRelayTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.service = StixRelay(str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db"))
        self.service.create_collection({"id": "feed", "title": "Primary feed"}, "c1")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def add(self, payload: dict, key: str, added_at: str = "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"):
        return self.service.add_object("feed", dict(payload, added_at=added_at), key).to_json()

    def add_status(self, payload: dict, key: str, added_at: str = "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z") -> int:
        return self.service.add_object(
            "feed", dict(payload, added_at=added_at), key
        ).status

    def test_collection_is_created_once_and_conflicts_on_duplicate(self):
        document = self.service.get_collection("feed")
        self.assertEqual("Primary feed", document["title"])
        self.assertEqual("application/stix+json;version=2.1", document["media_type"])
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "already exists"):
            self.service.create_collection({"id": "feed", "title": "Other"}, "c2")

    def test_object_round_trip_preserves_every_property(self):
        stored = self.add(indicator(), "k1")
        self.assertEqual("feed", stored["collection_id"])
        self.assertEqual("2024-01-02T00:00:00.000000Z", stored["added_at"])
        self.assertEqual("2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", stored["version"])
        self.assertEqual("[file:hashes.'SHA-256' = 'aa']", stored["object"]["pattern"])
        self.assertEqual("stix", stored["object"]["pattern_type"])
        self.assertEqual(
            [stored["object"]], self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"]
        )

    def test_timestamps_are_normalised_to_microsecond_utc(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1")
        document = self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"][0]
        self.assertEqual("2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", document["created"])
        self.assertEqual("2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", document["modified"])

    def test_unknown_property_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "unsupported properties: whatever"):
            self.add(dict(identity(), whatever=1), "k1")

    def test_unknown_type_is_rejected(self):
        payload = dict(identity(), type="campaign")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "type must be one of"):
            self.add(payload, "k1")

    def test_id_prefix_must_match_type(self):
        payload = dict(identity(), id=INDICATOR_ID)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "does not match type identity"):
            self.add(payload, "k1")

    def test_malformed_identifiers_are_rejected(self):
        for identifier in (
            "identity--f431f809-377b-15e0-aa1c-6a4751cae5ff",
            "identity--F431F809-377b-45e0-aa1c-6a4751cae5ff",
            "identity-f431f809-377b-45e0-aa1c-6a4751cae5ff",
        ):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "must be a STIX identifier"):
                self.add(dict(identity(), id=identifier), f"k-{identifier}")

    def test_required_properties_are_enforced_per_type(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "identity requires the name property"):
            self.add({key: value for key, value in identity().items() if key != "name"}, "k1")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "malware requires the is_family property"):
            self.add({key: value for key, value in malware().items() if key != "is_family"}, "k2")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "indicator requires the pattern property"):
            self.add({key: value for key, value in indicator().items() if key != "pattern"}, "k3")

    def test_property_types_are_enforced(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "is_family must be a boolean"):
            self.add(dict(malware(), is_family="yes"), "k1")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "labels must be a non-empty array"):
            self.add(dict(identity(), labels=[]), "k2")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "confidence must be an integer"):
            self.add(dict(identity(), confidence=101), "k3")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "external_references\\[0\\] must contain source_name"):
            self.add(dict(identity(), external_references=[{"url": "https://x"}]), "k4")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "kill_chain_phases\\[0\\] must contain exactly"):
            self.add(dict(malware(), kill_chain_phases=[{"kill_chain_name": "x"}]), "k5")

    def test_patterns_are_validated(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "must be a STIX pattern"):
            self.add(indicator(pattern="file:name = 'x'"), "k1")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "must be a STIX pattern"):
            self.add(indicator(pattern="[file:name = x]"), "k2")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "only pattern_type stix"):
            self.add(dict(indicator(), pattern_type="snort"), "k3")

    def test_spec_version_must_be_2_1(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "spec_version must be 2.1"):
            self.add(dict(identity(), spec_version="2.0"), "k1")

    def test_modified_cannot_precede_created(self):
        payload = dict(identity(), created="2024-05-05T00:00:00Z", modified=CREATED)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "modified must not be earlier than created"):
            self.add(payload, "k1")

    def test_relationship_endpoints_must_exist(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "unknown indicator"):
            self.add(relationship(), "k1")

    def test_relationship_endpoint_types_are_fixed(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "source_ref must reference a indicator"):
            self.add(dict(relationship(), source_ref=IDENTITY_ID, target_ref=INDICATOR_ID), "k1")

    def test_relationship_is_stored_once_both_endpoints_exist(self):
        self.add(indicator(), "k1")
        self.add(identity(), "k2")
        stored = self.add(relationship(), "k3")
        self.assertEqual("indicates", stored["object"]["relationship_type"])
        listed = self.service.list_objects("feed", ["relationship"]).to_json()
        self.assertEqual([stored["object"]], listed["objects"])
        self.assertEqual(["relationship"], listed["type"])

    def test_duplicate_relationship_is_rejected(self):
        self.add(indicator(), "k1")
        self.add(identity(), "k2")
        self.add(relationship(), "k3")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "already exists"):
            self.add(relationship(), "k4")

    def test_new_version_is_appended_and_old_version_is_read_only(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1", added_at="2024-01-02T00:00:00Z")
        self.add(
            identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z", name="Renamed Org"),
            "k2",
            added_at="2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        versions = self.service.object_versions("feed", IDENTITY_ID).to_json()
        self.assertEqual(
            ["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"], versions["versions"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z"], versions["earliest"])
        self.assertEqual(["2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"], versions["latest"])
        document = self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"][0]
        self.assertEqual("Renamed Org", document["name"])
        self.assertEqual("2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z", document["modified"])

    def test_version_must_advance(self):
        self.add(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z"), "k1")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "is older than the stored version"):
            self.add(identity(), "k2")

    def test_identical_version_is_a_conflict(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "already exists"):
            self.add(identity(), "k2")

    def test_versions_are_monotonic_and_unique(self):
        stamps = ["2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-03T00:00:00Z"]
        for index, stamp in enumerate(stamps):
            self.add(identity(modified=stamp), f"k{index}")
        versions = self.service.object_versions("feed", IDENTITY_ID).to_json()["versions"]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(versions), versions)
        self.assertEqual(len(set(versions)), len(versions))
        self.assertEqual(3, len(versions))

    def test_unknown_object_versions_are_not_found(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(NotFoundError, "was not found in collection"):
            self.service.object_versions("feed", MALWARE_ID)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- revocation

    def test_revoked_is_optional_and_not_emitted_when_omitted(self):
        stored = self.add(identity(), "k1")
        self.assertNotIn("revoked", stored["object"])
        listed = self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"][0]
        self.assertNotIn("revoked", listed)

    def test_explicit_revoked_false_is_stored_as_false(self):
        stored = self.add(dict(identity(), revoked=False), "k1")
        self.assertIs(stored["object"]["revoked"], False)
        self.assertIs(
            self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"][0]["revoked"], False
        )

    def test_a_first_version_may_be_born_revoked_for_historical_import(self):
        stored = self.add(revoked(identity()), "k1")
        self.assertIs(stored["object"]["revoked"], True)
        self.assertEqual(1, len(self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"]))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "is revoked"):
            self.add(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z"), "k2")

    def test_revoked_must_be_a_boolean(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "revoked must be a boolean"):
            self.add(dict(identity(), revoked="yes"), "k1")

    def test_a_later_revocation_version_is_stored(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1", added_at="2024-01-02T00:00:00Z")
        result = self.add(
            revoked(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z")),
            "k2",
            added_at="2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        self.assertIs(result["object"]["revoked"], True)
        self.assertEqual("2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z", result["version"])
        self.assertEqual("2024-02-02T00:00:00.000000Z", result["added_at"])
        current = self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"][0]
        self.assertIs(current["revoked"], True)
        self.assertEqual("2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z", current["modified"])

    def test_revocation_version_is_listed_in_versions_latest_and_added_at(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1", added_at="2024-01-02T00:00:00Z")
        self.add(
            revoked(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z")),
            "k2",
            added_at="2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        versions = self.service.object_versions("feed", IDENTITY_ID).to_json()
        self.assertEqual(
            [
                "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z",
                "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z",
            ],
            versions["versions"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(["2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"], versions["latest"])
        self.assertEqual(
            ["2024-01-02T00:00:00.000000Z", "2024-02-02T00:00:00.000000Z"],
            versions["added_at"],
        )

    def test_a_revocation_version_must_match_the_current_version_except_lifecycle_fields(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1", added_at="2024-01-02T00:00:00Z")
        cases = (
            (dict(name="Renamed Org"), "name"),
            (dict(identity_class="government"), "identity_class"),
            (dict(description="new"), "description"),
            (dict(confidence=50), "confidence"),
        )
        for index, (overrides, field) in enumerate(cases):
            payload = revoked(dict(identity(modified="2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"), **overrides))
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, field):
                self.add(payload, f"rev-bad-{index}")
        # Nothing was written: only the original version remains and the object is live.
        versions = self.service.object_versions("feed", IDENTITY_ID).to_json()
        self.assertEqual(["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z"], versions["versions"])
        self.assertNotIn(
            "revoked", self.service.list_objects("feed").to_json()["objects"][0]
        )

    def test_a_revocation_version_must_carry_a_later_modified(self):
        self.add(dict(identity(), revoked=False), "k1")
        # Same modified with revoked=true still follows the identical-version conflict.
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "already exists"):
            self.add(revoked(identity()), "k2")

    def test_a_normal_new_version_still_applies_before_revocation(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1", added_at="2024-01-02T00:00:00Z")
        self.add(
            identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z", name="Renamed Org"),
            "k2",
            added_at="2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        result = self.add(
            revoked(identity(modified="2024-03-01T00:00:00Z", name="Renamed Org")),
            "k3",
            added_at="2024-03-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        self.assertIs(result["object"]["revoked"], True)
        self.assertEqual("Renamed Org", result["object"]["name"])

    def test_once_revoked_any_later_write_is_a_conflict(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1")
        self.add(revoked(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z")), "k2")
        later = identity(modified="2024-03-01T00:00:00Z")
        attempts = (
            later,
            dict(later, revoked=False),
            {key: value for key, value in revoked(later).items() if key != "revoked"},
            dict(revoked(later), name="Something else"),
        )
        for index, payload in enumerate(attempts):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "is revoked"):
                self.add(payload, f"after-{index}")
        self.assertEqual(
            2, len(self.service.object_versions("feed", IDENTITY_ID).to_json()["versions"])
        )

    def test_same_or_earlier_modified_after_revocation_keeps_existing_conflict_wording(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1")
        self.add(revoked(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z")), "k2")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "already exists"):
            self.add(revoked(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z")), "k3")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ConflictError, "is older than the stored version"):
            self.add(revoked(identity(modified="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z")), "k4")

    def test_a_rejected_revocation_or_later_write_consumes_no_idempotency_key(self):
        self.add(identity(), "k1")
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.add(
                revoked(identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z", name="Changed")),
                "rev-key",

import json
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from stixrelay.server import Handler
from stixrelay.service import StixRelay
from test_service import (
    IDENTITY_ID,
    INDICATOR_ID,
    MALWARE_ID,
    NOTE_ID,
    REPORT_ID,
    identity,
    indicator,
    malware,
    note,
    report,
)

IDENTITY_ADDED_AT = "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"
IDENTITY_VERSION = "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z"


class HttpTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The HTTP surface exposes the same rules as the service object."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        Handler.service = StixRelay(str(Path(cls.directory.name) / "http.db"))
        cls.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        cls.base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{cls.server.server_address[1]}"
        cls.thread = threading.Thread(target=cls.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        cls.thread.start()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.server.shutdown()
        cls.server.server_close()
        cls.thread.join(timeout=5)
        cls.directory.cleanup()

    def request(self, method: str, path: str, body: dict | None = None, key: str | None = None):
        data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=data, method=method)
        request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        if key:
            request.add_header("Idempotency-Key", key)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            try:
                return error.code, json.loads(error.read())
            finally:
                error.close()

    def request_raw(self, path: str):
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, method="GET")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
                return response.status, response.headers.get("Content-Type"), response.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            try:
                return error.code, error.headers.get("Content-Type"), error.read()
            finally:
                error.close()

    def test_health(self):
        status, body = self.request("GET", "/health")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual({"status": "ok", "product": "stixrelay"}, body)

    def test_collection_and_object_flow(self):
        status, body = self.request(
            "POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "f1", "title": "Feed one"}, "h1"
        )
        self.assertEqual(201, status)
        self.assertEqual("f1", body["id"])
        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/f1")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual("Feed one", body["title"])

        status, body = self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections/f1/objects/",
            dict(identity(), added_at=IDENTITY_ADDED_AT),
            "h2",
        )
        self.assertEqual(201, status)
        self.assertEqual(IDENTITY_ID, body["object"]["id"])
        self.assertEqual("2024-01-02T00:00:00.000000Z", body["added_at"])
        self.assertEqual(IDENTITY_VERSION, body["version"])

        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/f1/objects/?type=identity")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual([IDENTITY_ID], [item["id"] for item in body["objects"]])
        self.assertEqual(["identity"], body["type"])

        status, body = self.request(
            "GET", "/taxii2/collections/f1/objects/?added_after=2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"
        )
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual([], body["objects"])

        status, body = self.request(
            "GET", f"/taxii2/collections/f1/objects/{IDENTITY_ID}/versions/"
        )
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual([IDENTITY_VERSION], body["versions"])
        self.assertEqual([IDENTITY_VERSION], body["latest"])

    def test_repeated_object_post_returns_the_first_result(self):
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "f2", "title": "Feed two"}, "h3")
        payload = dict(indicator(), added_at="2024-01-05T00:00:00Z")
        first = self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/f2/objects/", payload, "h4")
        repeated = self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/f2/objects/", payload, "h4")
        self.assertEqual(201, first[0])
        self.assertEqual(201, repeated[0])
        self.assertEqual(first[1], repeated[1])

    def test_errors_use_the_documented_shape(self):
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "f3", "title": "Feed three"}, "h5")
        status, body = self.request(
            "POST", "/taxii2/collections/f3/objects/", dict(identity(), id=MALWARE_ID), "h6"
        )
        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        self.assertEqual("validation_error", body["error"]["code"])
        self.assertIn("does not match type", body["error"]["message"])

        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/nope/objects/")
        self.assertEqual(404, status)
        self.assertEqual("not_found", body["error"]["code"])

        status, body = self.request("GET", "/nope")
        self.assertEqual(404, status)
        self.assertEqual("not_found", body["error"]["code"])

        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/f3/objects/?unknown=1")
        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        self.assertEqual("validation_error", body["error"]["code"])

        status, body = self.request(
            "POST", "/taxii2/collections/f3/objects/", dict(malware(), added_at="bad"), "h7"
        )
        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        self.assertEqual("validation_error", body["error"]["code"])

    def test_objects_path_without_a_trailing_slash_is_accepted(self):
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "f4", "title": "Feed four"}, "h8")
        status, body = self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections/f4/objects",
            dict(malware(), added_at="2024-01-06T00:00:00Z"),
            "h9",
        )
        self.assertEqual(201, status)
        self.assertEqual(MALWARE_ID, body["object"]["id"])
        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/f4/objects?type=malware")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual([MALWARE_ID], [item["id"] for item in body["objects"]])

    def test_collection_access_boundary(self):
        self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections",
            {"id": "hidden", "title": "Hidden", "can_read": False},
            "ha1",
        )
        self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections",
            {"id": "readonly", "title": "Read only", "can_write": False},
            "ha2",
        )

        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertNotIn("hidden", [item["id"] for item in body["collections"]])
        self.assertIn("readonly", [item["id"] for item in body["collections"]])

        for path in (
            "/taxii2/collections/hidden",
            "/taxii2/collections/hidden/objects/",
            f"/taxii2/collections/hidden/objects/{IDENTITY_ID}/versions/",
        ):
            status, body = self.request("GET", path)
            self.assertEqual(404, status, path)
            self.assertEqual(
                {"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "collection access is denied"}},
                body,
                path,
            )

        status, body = self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections/hidden/objects/",
            dict(identity(), added_at=IDENTITY_ADDED_AT),
            "ha3",
        )
        self.assertEqual(404, status)
        self.assertEqual("collection access is denied", body["error"]["message"])

        status, body = self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections/readonly/objects/",
            dict(identity(), added_at=IDENTITY_ADDED_AT),
            "ha4",
        )
        self.assertEqual(403, status)
        self.assertEqual(
            {"error": {"code": "forbidden", "message": "collection is not writable"}}, body
        )

        # The denied write consumed nothing: the same key works on a writable collection.
        self.request(
            "POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "writable", "title": "Writable"}, "ha5"
        )
        status, body = self.request(
            "POST",
            "/taxii2/collections/writable/objects/",
            dict(identity(), added_at=IDENTITY_ADDED_AT),
            "ha4",
        )
        self.assertEqual(201, status)

    def test_content_type_must_be_json(self):
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base + "/taxii2/collections", data=b"{}", method="POST"
        )
        request.add_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
        request.add_header("Idempotency-Key", "h10")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
                body = json.loads(response.read())
                status = response.status
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            try:
                status = error.code
                body = json.loads(error.read())
            finally:
                error.close()
        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        self.assertEqual("validation_error", body["error"]["code"])

    def test_pagination_walks_every_page_and_freezes_the_snapshot(self):
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "p1", "title": "Paged"}, "p0")
        for number, object_id in enumerate(
            (
                "indicator--a2f4b7d8-2c7e-4a4b-9d0e-0f6a1c9d3f01",
                "indicator--a2f4b7d8-2c7e-4a4b-9d0e-0f6a1c9d3f02",
                "indicator--a2f4b7d8-2c7e-4a4b-9d0e-0f6a1c9d3f03",
            ),
            start=1,
        ):
            payload = dict(indicator(), id=object_id, name=f"Paged {number}")
            payload["added_at"] = f"2024-04-{number:02d}T00:00:00Z"
            status, _ = self.request(
                "POST", "/taxii2/collections/p1/objects/", payload, f"p{number}"
            )
            self.assertEqual(201, status)

        status, first = self.request(
            "GET", "/taxii2/collections/p1/objects/?type=indicator&limit=2"
        )
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual(["Paged 1", "Paged 2"], [item["name"] for item in first["objects"]])
        self.assertTrue(first["more"])
        self.assertEqual(["indicator"], first["type"])
        self.assertIn("next", first)

        # An object arriving mid-walk does not enter the open snapshot.
        late = dict(
            indicator(),
            id="indicator--a2f4b7d8-2c7e-4a4b-9d0e-0f6a1c9d3f04",
            name="Paged 4",
            added_at="2024-05-01T00:00:00Z",
        )
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/p1/objects/", late, "p4")

        status, second = self.request(
            "GET", f"/taxii2/collections/p1/objects/?next={first['next']}"
        )
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual(["Paged 3"], [item["name"] for item in second["objects"]])
        self.assertFalse(second["more"])
        self.assertNotIn("next", second)
        self.assertEqual(["indicator"], second["type"])

        # Replaying the same cursor repeats the remaining page, not the first.
        status, replayed = self.request(
            "GET", f"/taxii2/collections/p1/objects/?next={first['next']}"
        )
        self.assertEqual(second["objects"], replayed["objects"])

        # Restarting from page one sees the late object.
        status, restarted = self.request(
            "GET", "/taxii2/collections/p1/objects/?limit=10"
        )
        self.assertEqual(4, len(restarted["objects"]))
        self.assertFalse(restarted["more"])

    def test_legacy_objects_call_has_no_pagination_fields(self):
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "p2", "title": "Legacy"}, "pl0")
        payload = dict(malware(), added_at="2024-06-01T00:00:00Z")
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/p2/objects/", payload, "pl1")
        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/p2/objects/")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual(1, len(body["objects"]))
        self.assertFalse(body["more"])
        self.assertNotIn("next", body)
        self.assertNotIn("type", body)

    def test_revocation_lifecycle_over_http(self):
        self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections", {"id": "rv", "title": "Revocations"}, "rv0")
        base = dict(identity(), added_at="2024-01-02T00:00:00Z")
        status, first = self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/", base, "rv1")
        self.assertEqual(201, status)
        self.assertNotIn("revoked", first["object"])

        # A revocation that also changes another property is a 400 and writes nothing.
        bad = dict(
            identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z", name="Changed"),
            revoked=True,
            added_at="2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        status, body = self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/", bad, "rv-bad")
        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        self.assertEqual("validation_error", body["error"]["code"])
        self.assertIn("name", body["error"]["message"])

        # The rejected key is reusable for the conforming revocation.
        good = dict(
            identity(modified="2024-02-01T00:00:00Z"),
            revoked=True,
            added_at="2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        )
        status, body = self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/", good, "rv-bad")
        self.assertEqual(201, status)
        self.assertIs(body["object"]["revoked"], True)
        self.assertEqual("2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z", body["version"])

        # The revoked object stays visible and is not hidden from listings.
        status, body = self.request("GET", "/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual([IDENTITY_ID], [item["id"] for item in body["objects"]])
        self.assertIs(body["objects"][0]["revoked"], True)

        status, body = self.request(
            "GET", f"/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/{IDENTITY_ID}/versions/"
        )
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual(
            ["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"],
            body["versions"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(["2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"], body["latest"])

        # Any later write is a 409 conflict, including one that un-revokes.
        for index, payload in enumerate(
            (
                dict(identity(modified="2024-03-01T00:00:00Z")),
                dict(identity(modified="2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"), revoked=False),
                dict(identity(modified="2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"), revoked=True, name="X"),
            )
        ):
            payload["added_at"] = "2024-03-02T00:00:00Z"
            status, error_body = self.request(
                "POST", "/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/", payload, f"rv-after-{index}"
            )
            self.assertEqual(409, status)
            self.assertEqual("conflict", error_body["error"]["code"])

        # Replaying the original successful key still returns the first response.
        status, replayed = self.request("POST", "/taxii2/collections/rv/objects/", base, "rv1")
        self.assertEqual(201, status)
        self.assertEqual(first, replayed)

    def test_export_versions_all_ordering_cutoff_and_revocations(self):
        self._seed_export_collection()
        status, _, raw = self.request_raw(
            "/taxii2/collections/ex1/export?versions=all"
        )
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        documents = json.loads(raw)["objects"]
        self.assertEqual(
            [
                (IDENTITY_ID, "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", None),
                (INDICATOR_ID, "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", None),
                (IDENTITY_ID, "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z", None),
                (IDENTITY_ID, "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000000Z", True),
            ],
            [
                (item["id"], item["modified"], item.get("revoked"))
                for item in documents
            ],
        )

```python
            # body is validated, so a bad body never reveals existence.
            self.service.get_collection(parts[2])
            body = self._body()
            return 200, self.service.match_indicators(parts[2], body)
```

Hmm, calling get_collection then match_indicators re-checks. Slightly awkward. Alternative: give StixRelay a small public method or just let match_indicators take the body and do the check, and in the handler parse body first. The requirement about access-first — the double-check approach is safest for the "malformed JSON + missing collection → 404" case. But is that case actually required? "访问检查先于请求体验证" — yes, explicitly. Malformed JSON is body validation in a broad sense. I'll do the handler-level pre-check.

Actually cleaner: `match_indicators` itself does `_require_readable` first (service-level guarantee), and the handler additionally calls... hmm, double DB read. It's fine — small.

Alternatively, handler does:

```python
self.service.get_collection(parts[2])  # 404 before body parsing
```

and match_indicators also checks (defense in depth, and direct service callers get correct behavior). Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtlety: `get_collection` returns the document; using it purely for the check is fine and reads naturally.

Now `_body()` content-type check: POST matches requires `Content-Type: application/json` — "沿用现有 JSON 内容类型" confirms reusing `_body()`.

Now, no Idempotency-Key required: we simply don't read the header. Good.

No DB state changes: match_indicators only reads. `_current_documents` uses `self.store.connection` directly without transaction. Good.

Now tests. I should add tests to tests/test_service.py and tests/test_http.py covering:

Service tests:
- basic equality match on string
- number comparisons <, >, <=, >=
- != semantics, type mismatch no match
- bool not number (e.g. pattern `[x:a = 1]` with observation True → no match; pattern `[x:a = true]` with obs 1 → no match)
- missing path → no match
- include_revoked default excludes revoked, true includes
- only current version checked (old version pattern not used)
- sorted by id, each indicator once
- empty result count 0
- validation errors: body not dict, missing observations, empty observations, observations not dict, empty-string key, bad value types (list, None, dict), include_revoked wrong type, unknown field
- access: missing/unreadable collection → NotFoundError, and access before validation (bad body + missing collection → NotFoundError)
- no state change: snapshots/idempotency/objects counts unchanged

HTTP tests:
- full flow POST /taxii2/collections/{id}/matches returns matches/count
- 404 for missing/hidden collection even with invalid body
- 400 validation errors shape
- no Idempotency-Key needed
- GET on matches → 404

1	# StixRelay
2	
3	StixRelay is a small STIX 2.1 object library with a TAXII 2.1 collection subset on
4	top of it. It stores threat-intelligence objects in SQLite, validates them against
5	the subset of STIX described below, keeps every revision of an object, and serves
6	current state and `added_after` deltas over a TAXII-shaped HTTP API.
7	
8	The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:
9	
10	- six object types: `identity`, `indicator`, `malware`, `relationship`,
11	  `report`, and `note`;
12	- every object is validated against a fixed property allowlist plus a required set
13	  that depends on its type, and its `id` must match its `type`;
14	- a `relationship` can only be stored once both endpoints already exist in the
15	  same collection;
16	- a `report` can only be stored when every entry of `object_refs` already exists
17	  as the current version of an `identity`, `indicator`, `malware`,
18	  `relationship`, or `note` object in the same collection;
19	- a `note` is an analyst annotation of an `identity`, `indicator`, `malware`,
20	  `relationship`, `report`, or another `note` already in the same collection;
21	- revisions are append only: a newer `modified` timestamp adds a version, the
22	  `modified` timestamp is the TAXII version identifier, and versions never regress;
23	- deltas use `added_after` as a **strictly half-open** interval over the time the
24	  server received a version;
25	- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result.
26	
27	## Requirements
28	
29	- Python 3.11 or newer
30	- no third-party runtime dependencies
31	
32	## Run the service
33	
34	```bash
35	PYTHONPATH=src python -m stixrelay.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database stixrelay.db
36	```
37	
38	The process prints `StixRelay listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it has
39	bound the port.
40	
41	## Data model
42	
43	### Collections
44	
45	A collection contains exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `can_read`, and
46	`can_write`; the stored document adds the fixed `media_type` of this release.
47	`description` defaults to `""`, and `can_read`/`can_write` default to `true`.
48	The flags are enforced on the server: a collection with `can_read: false` is
49	invisible — it is absent from the collection list, and every direct read or
50	write against it (collection, objects, versions) fails with the same
51	`not_found` as a collection that does not exist, so its existence is never
52	revealed. A readable collection with `can_write: false` rejects object POSTs
53	with `forbidden`. Access is checked before validation, idempotency, versioning,
54	and cursor handling, so a denied request stores nothing and does not consume
55	its idempotency key.
56	
57	```json
58	{
59	  "id": "feed",
60	  "title": "Primary feed",
61	  "description": "",
62	  "can_read": true,
63	  "can_write": true,
64	  "media_type": "application/stix+json;version=2.1"
65	}
66	```
67	
68	### Objects
69	
70	Every object carries these common properties: `type`, `spec_version`, `id`,
71	`created`, `modified`, `created_by_ref`, `revoked`, `labels`, `confidence`,
72	`lang`, `external_references`. Type specific properties and requirements:
73	
74	| type | required | optional |
75	| --- | --- | --- |
76	| `identity` | `name` | `description`, `identity_class`, `sectors`, `contact_information`, `roles` |
77	| `indicator` | `name`, `pattern`, `valid_from` | `description`, `pattern_type`, `pattern_version`, `valid_until`, `indicator_types`, `kill_chain_phases` |
78	| `malware` | `name`, `is_family` | `description`, `malware_types`, `aliases`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `kill_chain_phases` |
79	| `relationship` | `relationship_type`, `source_ref`, `target_ref` | `description`, `start_time`, `stop_time` |
80	| `report` | `name`, `published`, `object_refs` | `description`, `report_types` |
81	| `note` | `content`, `object_refs` | `abstract`, `authors` |
82	
83	Property rules:
84	
85	- `id` must be `<type>--<uuid>` where `<uuid>` is a lowercase RFC 4122 version 4
86	  UUID, and `<type>` must equal the object's `type`;
87	- `spec_version`, when present, must be `2.1`;
88	- `created` and `modified` are required UTC timestamps of the form
89	  `2024-01-02T03:04:05.000000Z` (a missing fractional part expands to six digits),
90	  and `modified` must not be earlier than `created`;
91	- `labels`, `sectors`, `indicator_types`, `malware_types`, `aliases`, and `roles`
92	  are non-empty arrays of non-empty strings; `confidence` is an integer between 0
93	  and 100; `external_references` is a non-empty array of objects containing
94	  `source_name` and optionally `description`, `url`, `external_id`;
95	  `kill_chain_phases` is a non-empty array of objects containing exactly
96	  `kill_chain_name` and `phase_name`;
97	- `pattern_type` must be `stix` (the default). `pattern` must be a
98	  single-comparison STIX pattern such as `[file:hashes.'SHA-256' = 'aa']`: an
99	  object path, a colon, a property path (quoted segments are allowed), one of
100	  `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, and a quoted string, number, or boolean value;
101	- `relationship_type` is a snake_case name such as `indicates` or `targets-x_1`;
102	- a `relationship` fixes the endpoint types of this release: `source_ref` must
103	  reference an `indicator` and `target_ref` must reference an `identity`. Both
104	  endpoints must already exist in the same collection, which is what makes the
105	  reference integrity check meaningful. If both `start_time` and `stop_time` are
106	  given, `start_time` must not be later;
107	- a `report` requires `published` (a UTC timestamp in the same format as
108	  `created`/`modified`) and `object_refs`: a non-empty array of STIX identifiers
109	  whose type prefix is `identity`, `indicator`, `malware`, `relationship`, or
110	  `note`. Entries must be well formed, must not repeat, and must not point at the
111	  report itself (a `report--` identifier is rejected). The optional `report_types`
112	  is a non-empty array of non-empty strings. At write time every entry must
113	  resolve to the current version of an object in the **same** collection; an
114	  unknown, cross-collection, duplicated, or self reference — together with an
115	  empty array — is a `validation_error` and the whole submission is rejected. A
116	  later report version may add or remove entries freely; each submission is
117	  checked against the objects current in the collection at that moment;
118	- a `note` requires `content` (a non-empty string) and `object_refs`: a
119	  non-empty, duplicate-free array of STIX identifiers whose type prefix is
120	  `identity`, `indicator`, `malware`, `relationship`, `report`, or `note`. The
121	  optional `abstract` is a non-empty string and the optional `authors` is a
122	  non-empty array of non-empty strings. Entries must be well formed, must not
123	  repeat, and must not point at the note itself. At write time every entry must
124	  resolve to the current version of an object in the **same** collection (a
125	  revoked target still counts as existing); an unknown, cross-collection,
126	  self, or duplicate reference, an unsupported type, or an empty array is a
127	  `validation_error` and the whole submission is rejected. A later note version
128	  may freely edit `content`/`abstract`/`authors` and add or remove references;
129	  each submission is re-checked against the objects current at that moment.
130	
131	Any property outside the allowlist for the object's type is rejected.
132	
133	### Versions
134	
135	The `modified` timestamp **is** the TAXII version identifier of a revision.
136	
137	- posting an object whose `modified` is greater than the stored version appends a
138	  new revision; older revisions stay readable and are never modified;
139	- posting the same `modified` again is a `conflict`, even when the body differs;
140	- posting a `modified` earlier than the stored version is a `conflict`, so the
141	  version sequence of an object only grows;
142	- `GET /objects/` and delta listings report the newest revision of each object;
143	  `GET /objects/{objectId}/versions/` reports every revision.
144	
145	### Revocation
146	
147	`revoked` is the object lifecycle flag, not an ordinary editable property.
148	
149	- the first version may omit `revoked`, set it explicitly to `false`, or set it to
150	  `true` when importing intelligence that is already revoked. An omitted flag is
151	  treated as `false` by lifecycle checks and is not added to the response;
152	- while the current version is not revoked, a normal new version follows the usual
153	  validation and monotonicity rules and may change any property;
154	- posting a later `modified` with `revoked` changing from `false` (or omitted) to
155	  `true` creates a **revocation version**. After normalisation every property and
156	  value except `modified` and `revoked` must be identical to the current version;
157	  otherwise the response is `400 validation_error` and no version is written;
158	- a successful revocation returns the usual `201` write response with
159	  `object.revoked` set to `true` and `version` equal to the normalised `modified`;
160	- a revocation version becomes the current version: it is never hidden, it appears
161	  in unpaginated and paginated object listings, enters strictly half-open
162	  `added_after` deltas at its own `added_at`, and is listed in `versions`,
163	  `latest`, and `added_at`. Historical versions stay untouched;
164	- a pagination snapshot keeps the revocation state it started with: a revocation
165	  received after the first paged request never enters that round's later pages;
166	- revocation never cascades: relationships, reports, and notes keep working, and
167	  a revoked object still counts as an existing object of the collection in the
168	  relationship, report, and note reference integrity checks;
169	- once the current version is revoked, **any** later write to that id in the
170	  collection is a `409 conflict` — a later `modified`, flipping `revoked` back to
171	  `false`, omitting `revoked`, or changing other properties alike. Writes with the
172	  same or an earlier `modified` keep their existing `conflict` semantics.
173	
174	A rejected revocation or a write rejected after revocation adds no version and
175	does not consume its idempotency key. Replaying a key whose first write succeeded
176	still returns that first response, even when the object has since been revoked.
177	
178	### `added_at`
179	
180	`added_at` is when the server received a version, with microsecond precision. It is
181	independent of the STIX `modified` timestamp, which describes when the producer
182	changed the object. A POST body may set it explicitly to make delta behaviour
183	reproducible in tests; when it is absent the server uses its own clock.
184	
185	## HTTP API
186	
187	All bodies are JSON and must be sent with `Content-Type: application/json`.
188	Unknown fields, unsupported query parameters, and unknown routes are rejected.
189	TAXII object paths are accepted with or without their trailing slash.
190	
191	State-changing POST requests require an `Idempotency-Key` header. Replaying a key
192	returns the first result and the status of the first request; reusing a key for a
193	different operation is a `conflict`.
194	
195	### Health
196	
197	```http
198	GET /health
199	```
200	
201	Returns `{"status":"ok","product":"stixrelay"}`.
202	
203	### Collections
204	
205	```http
206	POST /taxii2/collections
207	Idempotency-Key: collection-1
208	
209	{"id":"feed","title":"Primary feed"}
210	```
211	
212	Returns HTTP 201 with the stored collection; creating an existing id is a
213	`conflict`.
214	
215	```http
216	GET /taxii2/collections
217	GET /taxii2/collections/feed
218	```
219	
220	The first returns `{"collections":[...]}` sorted by `id`, limited to collections
221	with `can_read: true`; the second returns one collection. An unknown or
222	unreadable collection is `not_found` with the message
223	`collection access is denied`.
224	
225	### Add an object
226	
227	```http
228	POST /taxii2/collections/feed/objects/
229	Idempotency-Key: indicator-1
230	
231	{
232	  "type": "indicator",
233	  "spec_version": "2.1",
234	  "id": "indicator--a2f4b7d8-2c7e-4a4b-9d0e-6f6a1c9d3f21",
235	  "created": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
236	  "modified": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
237	  "name": "Bad hash",
238	  "pattern": "[file:hashes.'SHA-256' = 'aa']",
239	  "pattern_type": "stix",
240	  "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
241	  "added_at": "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"
242	}
243	```
244	
245	Returns HTTP 201 with the stored object plus its storage metadata:
246	
247	```json
248	{
249	  "collection_id": "feed",
250	  "added_at": "2024-01-02T00:00:00.000000Z",
251	  "version": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z",
252	  "spec_version": "2.1",
253	  "object": {"type": "indicator", "...": "the validated object"}
254	}
255	```
256	
257	`object` is the canonical form of the submission: `spec_version` is filled in,
258	timestamps are normalised, and `pattern_type` defaults to `stix`. A mismatched
259	`id` prefix, a missing required property, an unknown property, a `relationship`
260	whose endpoints do not exist, or a `report` or `note` whose `object_refs` do not
261	resolve in the same collection is a `validation_error`.
262	
263	### Read objects
264	
265	```http
266	GET /taxii2/collections/feed/objects/?type=indicator,malware&added_after=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
267	```
268	
269	The filter query parameters are optional and may appear at most once.
270	
271	- `type` is a comma separated list of supported object types; only those types are
272	  returned and the applied list is echoed back in `type`;
273	- `added_after` is a UTC timestamp and the interval is **strictly half-open**: a
274	  version whose `added_at` equals the cutoff is excluded, and only versions with a
275	  greater `added_at` are returned. Omitting it returns every object;
276	- when an object received a new version after the cutoff, the delta returns that
277	  newest version;
278	- results are the newest revision of each object, sorted by `added_at` and then by
279	  object id, so the same query always returns the same order.
280	
281	```json
282	{"objects":[{"type":"identity","id":"identity--...","...":"..."}],"more":false,"type":["identity"]}
283	```
284	
285	A request without `limit` (and without `next`) is the legacy, un-paginated read: it
286	returns every matching current revision, `more` is always `false`, and no `next` is
287	present.
288	
289	### Cursor pagination
290	
291	Add `limit` to page through a large collection instead of receiving every object at
292	once:
293	
294	```http
295	GET /taxii2/collections/feed/objects/?limit=100
296	```
297	
298	`limit` is a decimal integer between `1` and `200` and may appear at most once. The
299	first request takes the normal read path, so `type` and `added_after` keep their
300	exact existing semantics.
301	
302	- each response keeps `objects` and `more`; when a `type` filter was applied, the
303	  applied list is echoed in `type` on every page;
304	- while the current ordering has more rows, `more` is `true` and the response adds
305	  `next`, an opaque URL-safe cursor; on the last page `more` is `false` and `next`
306	  is absent;
307	- follow-up requests send **only** `next` — repeating `type`, `added_after`, or
308	  `limit` together with `next` is a `validation_error`. The server remembers the
309	  filter and page size from the first request:
310	
311	```http
312	GET /taxii2/collections/feed/objects/?next=v1.AbCd...
313	```
314	
315	- objects are ordered stably by `added_at` and then object id; each object appears
316	  at most once, showing only the newest revision readable in the pagination round;
317	- the first paged request establishes a **snapshot**. Objects and revisions
318	  received afterwards never enter that round's pages; they only become visible when
319	  a new round starts from page one. Replaying the same cursor re-reads the
320	  remaining pages of its own snapshot rather than restarting at the first page.
321	
322	`limit` that is not a decimal integer, is below `1`, above `200`, or appears more
323	than once is a `validation_error`. `next` that is repeated, malformed, issued by
324	another service, modified, bound to another collection, or combined with `type`,
325	`added_after`, or `limit` is also a `validation_error`.
326	
327	### Read object versions
328	
329	```http
330	GET /taxii2/collections/feed/objects/identity--f431f809-377b-45e0-aa1c-6a4751cae5ff/versions/
331	```
332	
333	Returns every revision of one object, oldest first:
334	
335	```json
336	{
337	  "id": "identity--f431f809-377b-45e0-aa1c-6a4751cae5ff",
338	  "versions": ["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"],
339	  "earliest": ["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z"],
340	  "latest": ["2024-02-01T00:00:00.000000Z"],
341	  "added_at": ["2024-01-02T00:00:00.000000Z", "2024-02-02T00:00:00.000000Z"]
342	}
343	```
344	
345	An object with no revision in that collection is `not_found`.
346	
347	### Export a collection
348	
349	```http
350	GET /taxii2/collections/feed/export/?format=stix&versions=current&type=indicator&added_after=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
351	```
352	
353	The path is accepted with or without its trailing slash. The export reuses the
354	existing collection read permission check (unknown or `can_read: false`
355	collections are the usual `404 not_found` with `collection access is denied`),
356	and `type` and `added_after` keep their exact validation and filtering
357	semantics from object reads. Two extra parameters are accepted, each at most
358	once:
359	
360	- `format` selects the rendering: `stix` (the default) or `ndjson`;
361	- `versions` selects which revisions are exported: `current` (the default) or
362	  `all`.
363	
364	`format=stix` returns `application/stix+json;version=2.1` with a body of only
365	`type` and `objects`:
366	
367	```json
368	{"type":"bundle","objects":[{"type":"indicator","...":"..."}]}
369	```
370	
371	Bundle members are the stored objects themselves; storage metadata
372	(`added_at`, `collection_id`, `version`) is never mixed into them. With no
373	results the bundle is `{"type":"bundle","objects":[]}`.
374	
375	`format=ndjson` returns `application/x-ndjson`: one complete object per line,
376	each line terminated by `\n`. With no results the body is zero bytes.
377	
378	Version modes:
379	
380	- `versions=current` exports the current version of each id, i.e. exactly the
381	  result set and order (`added_at`, then object id) of an unpaginated object
382	  read under the same `type`/`added_after` filter. A currently revoked object is
383	  exported;
384	- `versions=all` exports every matching historical revision. `added_after`
385	  applies strictly to each version's own `added_at`, results are ordered by
386	  `added_at`, object id, then `modified`, and each version appears once.
387	  Revocations are not hidden: the pre-revocation history is kept alongside the
388	  revoked current version.
389	
390	The two formats always express the same objects in the same order. An export is
391	read only: it starts no pagination snapshot, issues no cursor, writes no
392	version or idempotency record, and never modifies the database.
393	
394	Repeated or unsupported `format`/`versions`, an invalid `type` or
395	`added_after`, and `limit`, `next`, or any other unknown query parameter are
396	`400 validation_error`. Parameter validation runs only after the collection
397	read check, so a bad query against an unreadable collection stays `404`.
398	
399	## Errors
400	
401	Errors use this shape:
402	
403	```json
404	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
405	```
406	
407	Validation errors (unknown fields, unknown types, bad identifiers, bad patterns,
408	missing relationship endpoints, unresolvable report or note `object_refs`, a
409	revocation version that changes anything besides `modified` and `revoked`, bad
410	`added_after`, bad `limit` or `next`, unsupported query parameters) return 400. Writes to a read-only collection
411	return 403 (`forbidden`). Missing collections and objects — and any access to a
412	collection with `can_read: false` — return 404. Version conflicts, duplicate
413	collections, writes to an already revoked object, and idempotency key reuse
414	return 409.
415	
416	## Tests
417	
418	```bash
419	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
420	```
421	
422	`tests/test_service.py` covers object validation, version monotonicity, half-open
423	deltas, and idempotency. `tests/test_http.py` drives the real
424	`ThreadingHTTPServer` on an ephemeral port, including the error shapes.
425
